title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 3rd District
area: Western Twin Cities suburbs, including Minnetonka, Plymouth, Eden Prairie and Maple Grove.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Kelly Morrison (D) ran unopposed in the Democratic primary, winning 100% of the vote. Tyler Bass, a small-business owner, won the Republican primary over Quentin Wittrock, 55.4%-44.6%.

candidates.name: Kelly Morrison

summary.text: Kelly Morrison is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in Minnesota's 3rd Congressional District. She is a physician and former state legislator first elected to Congress in 2024.

background.text: Born in Minneapolis in 1969; earned a bachelor's degree in history from Yale University and an M.D. from Case Western Reserve University, and completed her residency in obstetrics and gynecology at Northwestern University.
Worked as a physician before entering politics.
Served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2019 to 2023, then in the Minnesota Senate from 2023 to 2024.

priorities.text: Kelly is committed to building an economy that works for everyone. This means lowering the cost of everyday needs such as health care, housing, and child care, while investing in innovation, infrastructure, and entrepreneurship.
Kelly is the first and only pro-choice OB-GYN in Congress and is fiercely committed to protecting reproductive rights.
As a doctor for more than 20 years, Kelly knows firsthand how critical access to healthcare is and it is a top priority for her.

positions.summary: Spoke on the House floor calling for an end to tariffs on Canadian goods, citing an estimated $4.8 billion cost to Minnesotans and job losses, and separately called on the Speaker to act on bipartisan bills to end the broader tariff war.
positions.quote: This will be a disaster for our small businesses, farmers, and every Minnesotan who is going to have to pay higher prices because of tariffs on everything from steel, to kitchen appliances, to hockey sticks.

positions.summary: Describes herself as the first and only pro-choice OB-GYN in Congress and introduced the SAFE Training for OB-GYNs Act to fund abortion-care training for OB-GYN residents in states with abortion bans.
positions.quote: As the only pro-choice OB-GYN in Congress, I know how important it is for OB-GYNs to receive hands-on experience in providing abortion care.

positions.summary: At a Small Business Committee hearing, criticized the administration for blocking the cheapest sources of new power and for repealing clean-energy tax incentives in the One Big Beautiful Bill, which she said will cost an estimated 500 gigawatts of new capacity over the next decade.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs; Health subcommittees) and the House Committee on Small Business (Contracting and Infrastructure; Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

Introduced the Safeguarding Access to Full-spectrum Education (SAFE) Training for OB-GYNs Act, June 24, 2026, to fund clinical abortion-care training for OB-GYN residents placed in states with abortion bans.
Sponsored the Native American Entrepreneurial Opportunity Act, which the U.S. House passed unanimously, June 24, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately. Positions and priorities above are drawn from her official House website's issue and press-release pages.

candidates.name: Tyler Bass
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary over Quentin Wittrock, 55.4%-44.6%.

summary.text: Tyler Bass is the Republican nominee challenging Rep. Kelly Morrison. He is a small-business owner from Minnetonka who grew up in Blooming Prairie, Minnesota.

background.text: Grew up in Blooming Prairie, Minnesota; earned a bachelor's degree from Luther College in 2010, where he studied exercise science and played college football.
Has worked as a general contractor; says he built a fitness-related business after struggling to find work following the 2011-2012 economic downturn.

priorities.text: Fighting government fraud: supports thorough investigations and oversight to stop misuse of public funds and benefit-program abuse before it happens.
Putting American workers first: supports holding large corporations accountable and requiring employers to prioritize hiring U.S. citizens, while barring employers from using undocumented labor.
Healthcare reform focused on prevention and affordability: supports lowering prescription drug prices and holding pharmaceutical and food companies accountable for chronic-disease-linked ingredients.

positions.summary: Supports enforcing existing immigration laws and making it impossible for employers to hire workers who are in the country illegally, while also supporting a faster legal path to citizenship for visa-holding immigrants.
positions.quote: On immigration, I support a faster and more efficient legal path to citizenship for visa-holding immigrants, while enforcing existing immigration laws.

positions.summary: Supports lowering prescription drug prices and holding pharmaceutical companies accountable, framed around prevention and food-industry regulation rather than expanding public coverage.
